Inherited Cowden phenotype includes cutaneous hamartomas and oral papillomatosis; thyroid cancer predisposition alone does not establish common thyroid damage in this subtype.
Branchial skin defects and ocular malformations define BOFS; hearing loss occurs in 5/6, and dental agenesis, microdontia and cleft lip in 30-79%; renal anomalies occur in 5-29%.

The syndromic intellectual disability parent establishes neurodevelopmental involvement; no additional organ phenotype is supplied.
Achalasia causes oesophageal dysfunction; alacrima is lacrimal dysfunction. Adrenal disease is not established by this two-feature syndrome.
Glycosylation disorder with severe neurologic disease; scoliosis 2/2 and hearing impairment 1/1. Optic disc pallor and retinal abnormalities 1/1 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Liver injury 21/21, cleft palate 25/32 and dilated cardiomyopathy 8/21; coagulation defects 40-50% omitted at cap. Elevated CK alone does not establish myopathy.
Acute myeloid neoplasm with marrow fibrosis and pancytopenia; weakness and fatigue do not establish muscle damage.
Brain malformation, congenital heart disease and polydactyly define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Common hair and nail abnormalities omitted at cap.
Single-gene diabetes affects endocrine pancreatic function; diabetic vascular, renal and retinal complications are separate diseases.
Inherited platelet and megakaryocyte disorder with anemia and marrow fibrosis; splenic involvement remains within the haematologic axis.
Dermatophytes invade the hair shaft; hair infection defines both axes.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy with ataxia and deficient or delayed dentition; hypogonadism is not established for this subtype.
Tumor arises from pancreatic endocrine cells and secretes serotonin; liver metastases and carcinoid complications are not defining organ involvement.
Umbrella for congenital infections; affected organs vary substantially by pathogen, with no additional organ established across most patients.
Craniosynostosis affects skull bones; Chiari I malformation and developmental and language delay establish neurologic disease.
Persistent ulceration directly damages skin; infection or vascular disease is not intrinsic to every chronic skin ulcer.
Corneal ulceration directly damages the eye; ring morphology alone does not establish an infectious or immune mechanism.
Neoplasm arising in the conus medullaris of the spinal cord.
Gastrointestinal juvenile polyps define the syndrome; cancer predisposition does not add another organ axis.
